With a gameplay centered around double-deck-building, be the first to get 10 gold ingots to be crowned ruler of GOLDblivion! In GOLDblivion, you have two decks of cards to manage: one for combat and one for development. Every turn starts by removing a card from your hand. This card is placed under a chosen section of your player board and will give a precious resource all game long! This process will also naturally clean your deck from bad cards. Combat is made by conquering territories represented by hexagonal tiles. The number of free spaces around a tile is the number of cards you draw from your combat deck to defeat the enemy under this territory. They get increasingly stronger and are more rewarding too! Based on the ever-changing cards in the market, develop a long-term strategy and find the best combinations between Elf, Dwarf, Human and Building cards to maximize your gold and be crowned King/Queen of GOLDblivion! Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 Overview 2 Setup 3 Round Overview 4 Player Turn Overview 5 Abilities 6 Combat 7 Tie Breaker 8 Solo Mode Overview GOLDblivion is a deck building game where each player gets two decks: one with GOLDblivion cards (blue) and one with Combat cards (red). The aim of the game is to get the most gold bars. When one player gets 10 or more gold bars, players play until the round is over and the player with the most gold bars wins! Players have two resources in the game: nuggets and material. Players are not limited for the number of nuggets they can have but they are limited to 4 material. Setup All players get the same starting GOLDblivion deck and Combat deck. At the start of the game, players select a Noble that they shuffle in their GOLDblivion deck. This is done in reverse turn order. Round Overview GOLDblivion is played in rounds. The game will end at the end of a round. The structure of a round is: Draw (all players simultaneously): All players draw 5 GOLDblivion cards from their deck. Development (all players simultaneously): All players must choose a card from their hand and place it in their Production area, either on the Produce Nugget side or the Produce Material side. The card remains faec-down; its power is not activated. Production (all players simultaneously): All players gain nuggets and materials depending on the number of cards in their Production area. Gain 1 nugget for each card in the Produce Nugget Side and 1 material for every 2 cards in the Produce Material Side (rounded down). Actions (each player in turn): Each player plays turns until all player have passed. End of round (all players simultaneously): Buildings are reactivated, cards are shuffled in their deck and magic tokens are shuffled face down. The First Player Token is passed to the next player; that player must destroy a card from the market. Player Turn Overview On their turn, players must play 2 main actions and any number of bonus actions. Main actions: Play a card: Play a card from your hand and activate the ability. (Note: Some abilities have a cost but you can play the card without paying its cost but you don’t activate the ability.) Buy a card: You pay the cost of the card in nuggets or material. If it’s a combat card, you shuffle it in your Combat deck. If it’s a GOLDblivion building card, you place it in your play area. If it’s a GOLDblivion card that is not a building, you shuffle it in your GOLDblivion deck. You cannot have the same building twice . Activate a village tile. You pay the cost and you activate the ability. You then flip the tile to reveal the other side. Pass. You must buy as many gold bars as you can (see the “Buy a gold bar” Bonus action). After you pass, you cannot do any other actions in this round. Bonus actions: Buy a gold bar: Pay 7 nuggets to buy a gold bar. Activate a building: Activate the building to activate its ability. [Rating: 3/10] Yet another soulless and repetitive deck building game about drawing and playing cards for different actions. Perhaps fans of this mechanic find unique aspects in Goldblivion but I got bored after one round.

[Rating: 4/10] There's a game in here on BGA but we've found it unclear and frustrating and my the way to bring it out.  I like deck building and get the premise but it's not helpful presently. Help me  Google AmassGames for more

[Rating: 4/10] I sincerely don't understand the high ratings of this game. Absolutely ordinary deckbuikding with terrible illustrations and "humor", huge amount of random and lack of balance starting from choosing a leader (get 1 gold or draw 1 card is a big difference). Yes, that game has some interesting ideas: two types of resources, a separate combat deck and magic tokens. But they are all undeveloped. It's even surprising me that GOLDblivion came out in 2023. In all aspects it resembles games from 10 years ago.

[Rating: 4/10] FIRST IMPRESSION:  Honestly, this might be a decent game but I could not get past the artwork which doesn't work for me. Probably one of my least favorite styles of artwork. Do be careful to keep purchasing cards so you don't run out since you trash a card every turn.

[Rating: 5/10] The decision of which card to sacrifice from your hand at the start of each turn is most interesting. It seems that some combinations of cards are so strong, generating coins or ingots, that others are not considered as possible purchases. For the same reason, the combat deck is left aside. There is no dependency between both decks. It would be nice if the resources generated with one were needed for the other or if there was synergy between both, this would make it more interesting to have to develop both.

[Rating: 5/10] Fine game with a fun loop. Tons of card culling from both decks you are building which feels great, but there is just 0 player interaction at all and that makes it hard for me to be interested in playing this game long term. The starter leader cards also feel imbalanced and the game does not look great.

[Rating: 5/10] Deck builder with silly cartoon. The gameplay is interesting, creating 2 decks does give more to think about, but the gameplay starts to feel too samey from game to game. I feel it could be done better, or allow for some more creative decisions. There are some moments of randomness with dice rolls, tile flips, card draws, that can frustrate. Overall, this is fun to play once, maybe twice, but I feel it doesn't have much staying power.
